gap: The reference sells speed with a heavy directional motion-blur streak trailing the whole body and a banked/dutch camera angle, while every one of our stills is a level, static-feeling shot of a vertical capsule with only a thin gas-puff contrail underneath — nothing about the frame itself implies velocity.

shots.note: ref reads faster: character is horizontal, cable taut on a steep diagonal with visible motion-streak trail; ours has a near-vertical capsule standing almost still with a slack-looking dual cable and no blur.
ref reads faster: banked camera plus a long white speed-streak sells the reel-in; ours shows a taut cable but the capsule and camera are static, so it reads as parked mid-air rather than reeling.

ref reads faster: dynamic pose with cloak flare and blur arc through the swing; ours has a visible gas-puff arc which is the strongest cue we have, but the capsule itself shows zero lean into the turn.

ref reads faster: the character's silhouette itself is angled into the arc with trailing blur; ours only implies the arc via a smoke trail while the rigid capsule stays upright, so the arc feels like a background effect, not body motion.
ref reads faster: thruster streaks read as propulsion off the anchor point; ours has a thicker gas puff which is decent, but the flat un-tilted camera and static capsule undercut the boost feeling.

ref reads faster even at rest: the pose still carries coiled tension and a fading blur trail from the prior motion; ours is a capsule standing dead-still on a rooftop with no impact dust, crouch, or residual trail, so it reads as idle, not just-landed.

ref reads faster: the taut cable-to-anchor plus blur sells momentum into the mantle; ours shows a nicely taut diagonal cable to two distinct anchor points, the best hook readability of the set, but the capsule itself has no motion cue.

reference: contact-odm-flight.jpg / odm-01..10 (odm-09 and odm-10 are the true flight frames; the rest are ground combat HUD screenshots)
